Scoring guide (out of 196):
  167-196 Ready for Stage 11 (advanced electives / honours).
  127-166 Nearly there — practise the topics of the missed questions for
          two weeks, then try those questions again.
  0-126   Keep working through Stage 10 (revise Stage 9 if needed); test
          again in a month.
  Compare the two parts: strong in B but weak in A means the student needs
  more practice writing proofs and explanations; strong in A but weak in B
  means more drill practice for speed and accuracy.


================================================================================
END OF STAGE 10 — READINESS CHECKLIST FOR STAGE 11
================================================================================
The student is ready for Stage 11 (final year / honours electives) when
they can usually:
  Analysis
  [ ] Use completeness, Bolzano-Weierstrass and Cauchy sequences to prove
      convergence, and prove continuity, uniform continuity and
      differentiability results rigorously
  [ ] Decide Riemann integrability, use Riemann-Stieltjes integrals, and
      test sequences and series of functions for uniform convergence
      (including the Weierstrass M-test)
  [ ] Work in metric spaces: open and closed sets, compactness,
      connectedness, completeness; apply the contraction mapping theorem,
      Arzela-Ascoli and Stone-Weierstrass
  [ ] Apply the inverse and implicit function theorems, and compute with
      differential forms and the generalised Stokes' theorem
  [ ] Test analyticity with the Cauchy-Riemann equations, use Cauchy's
      theorem and integral formula, and find Taylor and Laurent series
  [ ] Evaluate real integrals by residues and use conformal maps
  [ ] Compute Fourier series and transforms, solve Sturm-Liouville
      problems, and use Gamma, Beta, Legendre and Bessel functions
  [ ] Use Laplace, Fourier and Z-transforms, and solve simple integral
      equations
  Algebra
  [ ] Work with groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, cosets and Lagrange's
      theorem; normal subgroups, quotients and the isomorphism theorems
  [ ] Compute with permutations, use group actions (orbit-stabiliser,
      class equation) and the Sylow theorems
  [ ] Work with rings, ideals and quotient rings, and place a ring among
      integral domains, Euclidean domains, PIDs and UFDs
  [ ] Test polynomials for irreducibility (Eisenstein, reduction mod p)
  [ ] Compute degrees of field extensions and work in finite fields
  [ ] Find Galois groups of small polynomials, explain why the general
      quintic is not solvable by radicals, and decide constructibility
  [ ] Find Jordan forms and minimal polynomials, use the spectral theorem,
      diagonalise quadratic forms, and work with dual spaces and tensor
      products
  [ ] Decompose finitely generated modules over a PID (Smith normal form)
  [ ] Compute LU, QR and SVD decompositions and use them for least squares
      and PCA
  Geometry and topology
  [ ] Work with topological spaces, bases, continuity, product and
      quotient topologies, compactness, connectedness and separation
  [ ] Compute curvature, torsion, fundamental forms and Gaussian curvature,
      and apply Gauss-Bonnet
  [ ] Compute fundamental groups of simple spaces and use covering spaces
  [ ] Work in projective and hyperbolic geometry, use index notation and
      tensors, and compute fractal dimensions
  Applied and computational
  [ ] Solve the heat, wave and Laplace equations by separation of variables
      and first-order PDEs by characteristics
  [ ] Draw phase portraits, classify equilibria and recognise bifurcations
  [ ] Use numerical methods for roots, interpolation, integration, ODEs and
      linear systems, with error estimates
  [ ] Work with joint distributions, MGFs, the law of large numbers and the
      central limit theorem
  [ ] Estimate parameters (MLE), build confidence intervals, test
      hypotheses, fit regressions, and use Bayesian updating and simple
      time-series models
  [ ] Solve linear programmes by simplex and duality, recognise convex
      problems, and solve transportation, assignment, network-flow and
      queueing problems
  [ ] Find Nash equilibria (pure and mixed) and solve zero-sum games
  [ ] Write Lagrangians and Hamiltonians and solve Euler-Lagrange equations
  [ ] Count with inclusion-exclusion and Burnside/Polya, and reason about
      designs and Ramsey numbers
  [ ] Use propositional and predicate logic and explain completeness and
      Godel's incompleteness theorems
  [ ] Design automata, explain computability and the P vs NP question
  [ ] Use RSA, Diffie-Hellman and error-correcting codes
  [ ] Build, analyse and criticise mathematical models, and do basic
      financial and actuarial calculations
  [ ] Place the main ideas of mathematics in their history and discuss
      what mathematics is

Measure theory and Lebesgue integration, functional analysis, number
theory, manifolds and Lie groups, representation theory, stochastic
processes, dynamical systems and a first research project are the main
new work of Stage 11.
